title: Zanzibar Mix Plate
community: Zanzibar Stone Town — Forodhani Gardens evening market
author: Chef Fatuma
desc: Zanzibar Mix — the famous Forodhani night market platter. Mishkaki, bhajia, grilled octopus, coconut prawns, cassava chips, sugarcane juice, and an Urojo shot — everything the night market offers on one magnificent plate.
longDesc: The Zanzibar Mix is not a single dish — it is the Forodhani Gardens experience assembled on one plate. Each evening at the night market, visitors navigate between dozens of vendors, each specialising in one item. The Zanzibar Mix is the tourist and local shorthand for getting everything at once — a taste of every vendor's speciality.
ingredients: 100g cassava chips — deep fried from TZA010
4 large prawns — grilled with garlic butter (TZA067)
Cold sugarcane juice or tamarind drink
steps: Prepare each component from its individual recipe.
Stage the cooking: start with mishkaki over charcoal (longest).
Fry bhajias and cassava chips while mishkaki grills.
Cook prawns and squid last — they take under 5 minutes.
Arrange all components on a large platter or in individual bowls.
Serve with all sauces and fresh lime.
Everything must be hot — serve immediately.
chefTips: Staging is everything — the fastest-cooking items (squid, prawns) go on last.
Every component must be hot when served.
The cold drink is as important as the food — sugarcane juice or tamarind water.
commonMistakes: Cold components — everything must arrive hot.
Poor staging — some items ready before others.
cookingScience: See individual component recipes for cooking science.
sustainabilityTips: The Forodhani model — each vendor specialising in one item — is inherently sustainable, reducing waste and maximising quality.
culturalNote: The Zanzibar Mix represents the most famous food experience in Tanzania — the Forodhani Gardens night market, where the Indian Ocean breeze carries the smell of charcoal and spices, and every evening is a celebration of what Zanzibar has to offer the world.
